title: Desire
label: Columbia
note: Co-written largely with theater director Jacques Levy, with Scarlet Rivera's gypsy violin and Emmylou Harris's harmonies. The Rolling Thunder Revue's studio record.

tracks.note: A plea for boxer Rubin Carter, re-recorded after Columbia's lawyers objected to the first version's lyrics.
A marriage, a tomb, a treasure hunt. He played it in whiteface on the Rolling Thunder tour.

tracks.t: One More Cup of Coffee (Valley Below)
tracks.note: Written after a visit to a gypsy festival in Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer on his 34th birthday.
A ballad for the mobster Joey Gallo, which Lester Bangs called 'repellent romanticist bullshit'.
An island, a volcano and a Panama hat; the narrator learns of it all on the evening news.
Sung to his wife, who was in the studio, as their marriage was ending.

title: Street-Legal
label: Columbia
note: Big-band Dylan: horns, backing singers, apocalyptic imagery. Trashed at the time, rehabilitated since.

tracks.note: A Top 20 hit in the UK.

tracks.t: Where Are You Tonight? (Journey Through Dark Heat)

title: Slow Train Coming
label: Columbia
note: Recorded at Muscle Shoals with Mark Knopfler on guitar, after Dylan's born-again conversion. It won him his first solo Grammy.

tracks.note: Won the Grammy for Best Male Rock Vocal. John Lennon answered it with 'Serve Yourself'.

tracks.t: Gonna Change My Way of Thinking
Do Right to Me Baby (Do Unto Others)
Man Gave Names to All the Animals
tracks.note: A reggae nursery rhyme that stops before it names the snake.
Dylan alone with Barry Beckett's piano, singing a guide vocal he decided to keep.

title: Saved
label: Columbia
note: Full gospel, cut in five days with his touring band and backing singers. His lowest-charting album since 1964.

tracks.t: What Can I Do for You?

title: Shot of Love
label: Columbia
note: The last of the gospel trilogy, with the religion loosening its grip and 'Every Grain of Sand' at the end.

tracks.note: Ringo Starr and Ronnie Wood sat in on the take.
An elegy for the comedian, written years after his death. 'He was an outlaw, that's for sure.'

tracks.t: The Groom's Still Waiting at the Altar
tracks.note: Originally a B-side, added to the album in 1985.
A hymn out of William Blake. Sung at Johnny Cash's funeral by Emmylou Harris and Sheryl Crow.

title: Infidels
label: Columbia
note: With Knopfler, Mick Taylor and the rhythm section of Sly and Robbie. Famous as much for what it left off: 'Blind Willie McTell' and 'Foot of Pride'.

tracks.note: 'Standing on the waters casting your bread.' Revisited on the first Bootleg Series with an entirely different lyric.
Performed on Late Night with David Letterman in 1984 with a punk band, the Plugz.

tracks.t: Don't Fall Apart on Me Tonight

title: Empire Burlesque
label: Columbia
note: Mixed by Arthur Baker in the full gated-reverb style of 1985. Lyrics woven with lines lifted from Humphrey Bogart films.

tracks.t: Tight Connection to My Heart (Has Anybody Seen My Love)
tracks.note: Rebuilt from the Infidels outtake 'Someone's Got a Hold of My Heart'.

tracks.t: Seeing the Real You at Last
Never Gonna Be the Same Again
When the Night Comes Falling from the Sky
tracks.note: An earlier take with Steve Van Zandt and Roy Bittan of the E Street Band surfaced on the Bootleg Series.
Acoustic, written overnight after the producer asked for one more song.

title: Knocked Out Loaded
label: Columbia
note: Thirty-five minutes of odds and ends, redeemed by one eleven-minute masterpiece written with Sam Shepard.

tracks.note: A half-remembered Gregory Peck western, a trip through Texas, and a Mexican backing choir. Reworked from 'New Danville Girl'.

title: Down in the Groove
label: Columbia
note: Covers, two co-writes with the Grateful Dead's Robert Hunter, and a guest list from Eric Clapton to Jerry Garcia. Dylan's commercial nadir.

tracks.w: Arthur Alexander / Earl Montgomery / Tom Stafford

tracks.note: An Infidels outtake. Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds covered it with Kylie Minogue and PJ Harvey.

tracks.t: Had a Dream About You, Baby

tracks.note: With the Grateful Dead on backing vocals. A live staple for the next fifteen years.

tracks.t: Ninety Miles an Hour (Down a Dead End Street)

title: Oh Mercy
label: Columbia
note: Recorded in a New Orleans mansion with Daniel Lanois. The comeback, told at length in Dylan's 'Chronicles'.

tracks.t: Man in the Long Black Coat
tracks.note: Lanois's swamp noir; crickets recorded on the porch.
Used in 'High Fidelity'. 'I don't even notice she's gone, most of the time.'

title: Under the Red Sky
label: Columbia
producer: Don Was, David Was, Bob Dylan
note: Nursery-rhyme songs dedicated to 'Gabby Goo Goo', his four-year-old daughter, with George Harrison, Elton John, Slash and Stevie Ray Vaughan dropping by.

tracks.note: Slash plays on it. Regularly listed among the worst Dylan songs, and performed anyway.
George Harrison on slide guitar.
Elton John on piano.

title: Good as I Been to You
label: Columbia
note: Solo acoustic folk and blues, recorded in his garage. The first album of no originals since 'Dylan'. A reset.

tracks.t: Sittin' on Top of the World

title: World Gone Wrong
label: Columbia
note: More solo acoustic traditionals, with Dylan's own cranky, brilliant liner notes. Won the Grammy for Best Traditional Folk Album.

title: Time Out of Mind
label: Columbia
note: Seven years without new songs, then this: mortality, Miami heat, Lanois murk. Album of the Year at the Grammys.

tracks.note: He was performing it at the Grammys when the 'Soy Bomb' dancer jumped onstage.

tracks.t: 'Til I Fell in Love with You

tracks.note: 'It's not dark yet, but it's getting there.'
Won the Grammy for Best Male Rock Vocal Performance.
Billy Joel released it first; Garth Brooks and then Adele made it a standard.
His longest studio recording until 'Murder Most Foul'. Features a conversation with a waitress in a Boston restaurant.

title: "Love and Theft"
label: Columbia
note: Released on September 11, 2001. Self-produced under the name Jack Frost, with his road band: jump blues, crooner ballads, rockabilly, and lines borrowed from a Japanese gangster memoir.

tracks.note: Written for Time Out of Mind and abandoned there; Sheryl Crow recorded it first.

title: Modern Times
label: Columbia
note: His first No. 1 album in thirty years, making him, at 65, the oldest living artist to top the Billboard chart at the time.

tracks.note: Name-checks Alicia Keys in the second verse.
Built on the Muddy Waters / Hambone Willie Newbern blues.
Won the Grammy for Best Solo Rock Vocal Performance.
A sequel, in spirit, to Merle Haggard's 'Workin' Man Blues'.

title: Together Through Life
label: Columbia
note: Tex-Mex accordion from David Hidalgo of Los Lobos; lyrics co-written with Robert Hunter. It began as a single song for a French film.

tracks.note: The song written for Olivier Dahan's 'My Own Love Song' that grew into the album.

tracks.w: Bob Dylan / Robert Hunter / Willie Dixon

tracks.t: If You Ever Go to Houston
I Feel a Change Comin' On

title: Christmas in the Heart
label: Columbia
note: Fifteen Christmas standards, sung in the full late-period rasp. All royalties go to food charities, in perpetuity.

tracks.t: Do You Hear What I Hear?

tracks.w: Kim Gannon / Walter Kent / Buck Ram

tracks.t: O' Come All Ye Faithful (Adeste Fideles)
tracks.note: The first verse is sung in Latin.

tracks.t: Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas

tracks.note: A polka. The video, with Dylan in a long wig at a house party, is a small masterpiece of chaos.

title: Tempest
label: Columbia
note: Released fifty years after his debut. Blood-soaked ballads, a fourteen-minute Titanic, and a farewell to John Lennon.

tracks.note: 'I pay in blood, but not my own.'
Forty-five verses on the sinking of the Titanic, with Leonardo DiCaprio among the passengers.
An elegy for John Lennon, quoting 'A Day in the Life' and 'Come Together'.

title: Shadows in the Night
label: Columbia
note: Ten songs Frank Sinatra recorded, cut live with a five-piece band and no headphones. 'I'm not covering these songs. They've been covered enough. I'm uncovering them.'

tracks.t: I'm a Fool to Want You
tracks.w: Frank Sinatra / Jack Wolf / Joel Herron

tracks.t: The Night We Called It a Day

tracks.w: Joseph Kosma / Johnny Mercer / Jacques Prévert

tracks.t: Why Try to Change Me Now

title: Fallen Angels
label: Columbia
note: A second helping of standards, released days before his 75th birthday and months before the Nobel Prize.

tracks.note: The only song on the album Sinatra never recorded.

tracks.t: On a Little Street in Singapore

title: Triplicate
label: Columbia
note: Three discs of ten standards each, 32 minutes apiece, titled ''Til the Sun Goes Down', 'Devil Dolls' and 'Comin' Home'. His first triple album.

tracks.t: I Guess I'll Have to Change My Plans
The Best Is Yet to Come
There's a Flaw in My Flue
I Couldn't Sleep a Wink Last Night

tracks.w: Les Brown / Ben Homer / Bud Green

tracks.t: It's Funny to Everyone but Me

title: Rough and Rowdy Ways
label: Columbia
note: His first album of originals in eight years, released into the pandemic at 79. Whitman, Frankenstein, Dallas 1963 and the ghosts of Key West.

tracks.note: 'I'm just like Anne Frank, like Indiana Jones, and them British bad boys, the Rolling Stones.'
Built on Billy 'The Kid' Emerson's 1954 Sun single 'If Lovin' Is Believing'.
A Frankenstein story: assembling a companion from limbs and brains, Al Pacino and Marlon Brando.

tracks.t: I've Made Up My Mind to Give Myself to You

tracks.note: Seventeen minutes on the Kennedy assassination and the songs that followed it. His first No. 1 single on any Billboard chart, released at midnight with no warning in March 2020.
